claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's helpful to know that Alex is 8 years old and lives with you in the UK.

To continue assessing your eligibility, I need to ask:

**Are you responsible for Alex's day-to-day care? For example, do you provide for his food, clothes, and other daily needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I take care of him day-to-day - I provide his food, clothes, and everything else he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great. Now I need to understand a bit more about your living situation:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just one more question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex in any of the following situations:**
- In hospital or residential accommodation for more than 12 weeks?
- In care (provided by the local council) for more than 8 weeks?
- Working 24 hours or more per week?
- Receiving benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, yes - Alex has been in hospital for a few months now. It's been quite difficult.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to hear that Alex has been in hospital - that must be very difficult for you and your family.

To properly assess how this affects your Child Benefit eligibility, I need to know:

**How many weeks has Alex been in hospital? And during this time, have you been regularly spending money on him (for example, on clothes, toys, treats, or other items for him)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in hospital for about 15 weeks now. As for spending money on him... well, I'm not really sure how to answer that. With everything going on, I haven't really kept track of whether I've been buying him things regularly or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - it's a very stressful time and keeping track of such details can be difficult.

Let me ask this in a simpler way: **During these 15 weeks that Alex has been in hospital, have you bought him things like toys, books, clothes, snacks, or other items? Even if you're not sure about the frequency, has there been any spending on items for him during his hospital stay?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: To be honest, I really can't say for certain. It's all been a bit of a blur with everything that's been happening.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand - it's an incredibly stressful situation and it's understandable that you haven't been tracking these details.

Based on the information you've provided, let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I cannot make a definitive determination about your Child Benefit eligibility for Alex at this time.

**Here's the situation:**

You meet the basic criteria for Child Benefit - Alex is 8 years old, lives with you in the UK, you're responsible for his care, and no one else is claiming for him. Under normal circumstances, you would be eligible.

**However**, there's an important factor: Alex has been in hospital for about 15 weeks, which is longer than the 12-week threshold. According to the rules, after 12 weeks in hospital, Child Benefit can usually continue **if you regularly spend money on your child** (for example, on clothes, toys, books, or other items for them).

Since you're understandably unsure whether you've been regularly spending money on Alex during his hospital stay, I cannot definitively determine if you qualify for this exception.

**What I'd recommend:** Contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly to discuss your specific circumstances. They can review your situation in detail and help determine whether the exception applies to you. They're best positioned to consider all the factors and make a final decision about your entitlement.

I hope Alex recovers soon, and I wish you and your family all the best during this difficult time.
